question.text: As per IAS 39 and AS 30, which of the following is NOT a required criterion for a financial derivative?

answer.text: Trade must settle on net basis and not on gross basis
Value of derivative is linked to the value of underlying
Trade settled on a future date
On trade date, there should be no full cash outlay

explanation.text: The Logic: Under IAS 39 and AS 30, a derivative is characterised by (1) value linked to an underlying, (2) settlement on a future date, and (3) no full cash outlay on trade date. Net settlement is an additional criterion under FAS 133, not under IAS 39 or AS 30. The Trap: All four options sound like reasonable derivative features, but only three are required under IAS 39 and AS 30; net settlement belongs to FAS 133. Note: The "no full cash outlay" criterion is what provides leverage in derivatives, allowing exposure without the full underlying payment upfront. Source: page 35 of the NISM Series-I workbook.
